answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a inlet as the anchor of the cost.
